# Chapter 5 — Disaster Recovery and Platform Resilience

The UIAO platform's disaster recovery posture reflects the same governance discipline applied to the modernization pipeline itself. Every recovery procedure is documented, deterministic, and executable by any authorized administrator — not just the person who built the system. This is a design requirement, not a documentation courtesy. A governance platform whose recovery depends on the institutional knowledge of a single individual is not a governance platform; it is a single point of failure with documentation theater attached to it.

The DR playbook covers twelve platform components in explicit detail: the Gitea application server configuration and binary, the IIS reverse proxy configuration including ARR and URL Rewrite rules, all bare Git repositories and their hook scripts, the Gitea SQLite database, the Active Directory assessment JSON output store, the PKI and TLS certificate chain, the canonical governance artifacts in the canon/ directory, the Quarto-rendered documentation output, the governance hooks across all repositories, the PowerShell assessment and utility modules, the replication infrastructure including scheduled tasks and mirror credentials, and the audit logs that provide the tamper-evident operational record.

Recovery objectives are defined explicitly and validated through quarterly drills. The Recovery Point Objective — the maximum acceptable data loss — is four hours, reflecting the combination of the six-hour GitHub mirror synchronization cycle and the scheduled assessment commit frequency. In practice, the most recent commit in the GitHub mirror will be no more than four hours old at any point in the day. The Recovery Time Objective — the maximum elapsed time to restore full platform functionality — is eight hours for a complete server loss scenario, assuming the secondary server is available and the most recent mirror synchronization has completed. Both objectives are validated through quarterly DR drills that execute the recovery runbooks against the secondary server and verify that the restored environment passes the full platform validation test suite before the drill is marked successful.

The backup architecture uses Windows Scheduled Tasks in the \UIAO\\ task folder to orchestrate four scheduled operations: a nightly full backup of the Gitea data directory and SQLite database; a nightly backup of the D:\UIAO\\ assessment and module directories; a nightly push of all governance repositories to the secondary server mirror via authenticated Git remote; and a six-hourly push to the GitHub external mirror. Backups are stored in a versioned directory structure under D:\UIAO\Backups\\ with timestamped subdirectories and a JSON manifest file recording the backup scope, duration, component list, and hash verification results for every backed-up file. Backup integrity verification runs as a separate scheduled task the morning after each nightly backup, and any verification failure generates an immediate alert to the platform monitoring dashboard.
